Prevention: Do not establish papaya crop in high humidity areas with temperatures below 24°C Plant in rows parallel to prevailing wind and avoid overcrowding to increase air movement in the canopy
Avoid overhead irrigation to reduce humidity which promotes disease spread
Avoid intercropping with susceptible crops such as cucumber or pumpkin
Monitoring: Water soaked spots with white powdery patches mainly along the leaf veins, leaf petioles, flower pedicels, and at peduncles on the stem, on lower and upper sides of the leaves
Signs of necrotic and scotched leaves
Circular white patches on the surface of fruits
Take action when disease symptoms are observed on one plant
Direct Control: Collect and dispose of any fallen leaves by burying or burning
Do not use the collected leaves for composting
Spray using baking powder, neem extracts and white mineral oil plus soap solution are alternatives for control
Water the crop early in the day at the root zone
Restrictions: Read the label and follow manufacturer’s instructions carefully before use
When using a pesticide always wear protective clothing.
Follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre- harvest interval, max number of sprays, restricted re-entry interval.
